name: GGUF Q3_K_M (3-bit K-quant, medium)
quality_delta: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, one checkpoint, official llama.cpp toolchain, vs its own F16 baseline (quant-gguf-kquant-study): WikiText-2 ppl 7.96 vs 7.32 (+0.64); GSM8K 75.03 vs 77.63 (-2.60); HellaSwag 73.16 vs 72.51; IFEval 73.41 vs 78.93; MMLU 77.19 vs 63.50; TruthfulQA 54.56 vs 54.79; unweighted mean 68.07 vs 69.47. Size 3825 MiB vs 15317 MiB F16 (-75.03%).
notes: Bits is not 3.0: at 3.9960 bpw Q3_K_M is measurably wider than a nominal 4-bit format, which is why llama.cpp's own bit table lists it alongside 4-bit-class sizes. Q3_K_M is the study's recommended 'safer 3-bit' choice and sits on the size/quality Pareto frontier (75.03% reduction, AvgLoss -2.02%). Weight-only: activations stay in FP16/BF16 at runtime, so there is no '4-bit activations with hardware support' claim to make here. ggml has bespoke dequantize+gemm kernels per type, but no accelerator has a GGUF/k-quant path in silicon; everything is dequantized on the fly. vLLM explicitly labels its GGUF support experimental and under-optimized and positions it as a memory-footprint tool (quant-vllm-gguf-doc). Contested caveat: the same study reports Q3_K_L at 4.2979 bpw in its own prose (quant-gguf-kquant-study), so quoted '3-bit' bpw figures for the family are inconsistent across sources - trust the per-type table in quant-llamacpp-quantize-readme over round numbers.
